```{r}
Q1 <- quantile(data$money_deal, 0.25)
Q3 <- quantile(data$money_deal, 0.75)
IQR_value <- Q3-Q1

lower_limit <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_value
upper_limit <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_value
mild_outliers <- data[data$money_deal < lower_limit | data$money_deal > upper_limit, ]

df<-subset(data,lower_limit <= money_deal &  money_deal <= upper_limit)
df
```


# Statistical Inference
## Paired t-test
```{r}
# Extract data from 2020/6/3 to 2020/6/18
start_date_1 <- as.Date("2020-06-18") - 15
end_date_1 <- as.Date("2020-06-18") 
data_1 <- data[(data$Date >= start_date_1 & data$Date <= end_date_1), ]

# Extract data from 2019/10/27 to 2019/11/11
start_date_2 <- as.Date("2019-11-11")  - 15
end_date_2 <- as.Date("2019-11-11") 
data_2 <- data[(data$Date >= start_date_2 & data$Date <= end_date_2), ]

# Make sure the number of rows are the same
if (nrow(data_1) == nrow(data_2)) {
  # paired test
  paired_test_result <- t.test(data_1$money_deal, data_2$money_deal, paired = TRUE, alternative = "less")
  print(paired_test_result)
} else {
  print("The number of rows are not the same. Paired test cannot be done.")
}
```

## ANOVA
```{r}
# Date Range 1: From 2019-06-01 to 2019-08-31
start_date_1 <- as.Date("2019-06-01")
end_date_1 <- as.Date("2019-08-31")
data_1 <- data[(data$Date >= start_date_1 & data$Date <= end_date_1), ]

# Date Range 2: From 2019-09-01 to 2019-11-30
start_date_2 <- as.Date("2019-09-01")
end_date_2 <- as.Date("2019-11-30")
data_2 <- data[(data$Date >= start_date_2 & data$Date <= end_date_2), ]

# Date Range 3: From 2019-12-01 to 2020-02-29
start_date_3 <- as.Date("2019-12-01")
end_date_3 <- as.Date("2020-02-29")
data_3 <- data[(data$Date >= start_date_3 & data$Date <= end_date_3), ]

# Date Range 4: From 2020-03-01 to 2020-05-31
start_date_4 <- as.Date("2020-03-01")
end_date_4 <- as.Date("2020-05-31")
data_4 <- data[(data$Date >= start_date_4 & data$Date <= end_date_4), ]

# Date Range 5: From 2020-06-01 to 2020-08-20
start_date_5 <- as.Date("2020-06-01")
end_date_5 <- as.Date("2020-08-20")
data_5 <- data[(data$Date >= start_date_5 & data$Date <= end_date_5), ]

# Combine the data and add a grouping factor
data_combined <- rbind(
  data.frame(data_1, group = "2019-06 to 2019-08"),  # Group 1
  data.frame(data_2, group = "2019-09 to 2019-11"),  # Group 2
  data.frame(data_3, group = "2019-12 to 2020-02"),  # Group 3
  data.frame(data_4, group = "2020-03 to 2020-05"),   # Group 4
  data.frame(data_5, group = "2020-06 to 2020-08")   # Group 5
)

# Perform One-Way ANOVA on 'money_deal' with 'group' as the independent variable
anova_result <- aov(money_deal ~ group, data = data_combined)

# Output the summary of the ANOVA test result
summary(anova_result)


```
```{r}
# Calculate the average 'money_deal' for each group
grouped_data <- data_combined %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(avg_money_deal = mean(money_deal, na.rm = TRUE))

# Create a bar plot to visualize the average 'money_deal' for each date range
ggplot(grouped_data, aes(x = group, y = avg_money_deal, fill = group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black") +  # Use 'identity' to make the height of the bars represent the calculated mean
  theme_minimal() +  # Apply a minimal theme to the plot
  labs(title = "Average Money Deal by Date Range", x = "Date Range", y = "Average Money Deal") +  # Add labels and title
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability

```
# linear regression
```{r}
data %>% ggpairs()
```

```{r}
qqplot(x = data$count_view, y = df$money_deal)
```


Correlations to choose best variables for money_deal to do linear regression
```{r}
ggcorr(data %>% select_if(is.numeric), digits = 12, label = TRUE, name = "Correlations", label_alpha = TRUE)
```


linear regression
```{r}
model <- lm(formula = money_deal ~ count_view * bounce_rate * count_visitor, data = df)
summary(model)
```


Non-constant Variance Test to check Homoscedasticity
```{r}
ncvTest(model)
```


F test for linear regression model
```{r}
f_test_result <- anova(model)
print(f_test_result)
```

```{r}
# View model summary
summary(model)

# Obtain residuals
residuals <- residuals(model)

# Plot residuals vs fitted values
ggplot(data, aes(x = fitted(model), y = residuals)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values", x = "Fitted values", y = "Residuals")

# Plot residuals vs time
ggplot(data, aes(x = Date, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Time", x = "Time", y = "Residuals")

# Use auto.arima to fit an ARIMA model to explore the impact of time factors
# First, convert residuals to a time series object
residuals_ts <- ts(residuals, frequency = 1) # Assuming one observation per year

# Fit ARIMA model
arima_model <- auto.arima(residuals_ts)

# View ARIMA model summary
summary(arima_model)

```
